lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Measurement: Time, Liquid Volume, and Mass
lessonRef.focus: measuring safely with an adult at home
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: measuring safely with an adult at home

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: A jug has 350 milliliters. Another 120 milliliters are poured in. How much is in the jug now?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A container has 218 milliliters. Another 33 milliliters are poured in. How many milliliters are in the container now?
A container has 346 milliliters. 173 milliliters are removed. How many milliliters are left?
A container has 309 milliliters. Another 262 milliliters are poured in. How many milliliters are in the container now?
A container has 793 kilograms. 273 kilograms are removed. How many kilograms are left?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A container has 303 kilograms. 300 kilograms are removed. How many kilograms are left?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A container has 514 kilograms. 208 kilograms are removed. How many kilograms are left?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
